This script will relate the DDM parameters for each subject with their ideological variables.

# Libraries

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(data.table)
```


# Import Data

```{r}
# Load and prepare data
behavior_path <- "C:/Users/Brian Kim/Documents/OneDrive - Drexel University/Documents/classes/cognew/Neuroethics/IndividualDifferenceRiskBenefit/DATA_ANALYSIS/data/FINAL_RT_EXCLUDED_DATA_20241014.RData"
load(behavior_path)

# Data preprocessing
risk_data <- risk_data %>%
  mutate(
    rt = rt / 1000, # Convert reaction time to seconds
    response = ifelse(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment", 1, 0),
    RT = if_else(response == 0, -rt, rt), # Negative RT for 'No' responses
    risk = risk * 0.01, # Convert percentages to proportions
    gain = gain * 0.01,
    no_effect = no_effect * 0.01,
    idxP = as.numeric(as.factor(user_id)) # Create numeric subject index
  ) 

ddm_path <- "C:/Users/Brian Kim/Documents/OneDrive - Drexel University/Documents/classes/cognew/Neuroethics/IndividualDifferenceRiskBenefit/DATA_ANALYSIS/analysis/finalDDM/NeuroethicsPosteriorAndPredictions.RData"

```

## Clean DDM Data

```{r}
# Extract DDM Metrics
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

# Step 1: Identify columns with square brackets in m1_posterior
# Extract columns that match the pattern with ".p[XX]" or just "[XX]"
selected_columns <- m1_posterior %>%
  select(matches("\\[\\d+\\]$"))

# Step 2: Calculate the averages for each column
averages <- selected_columns %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean, na.rm = TRUE))

# Step 3: Extract both metric_name and participant_id, handling both ".p[XX]" and "[XX]"
column_info <- tibble(
  full_colname = colnames(averages),
  participant_id = str_extract(colnames(averages), "(?<=\\[)\\d+(?=\\])"),  # Extract participant ID if present in square brackets
  metric_name = str_replace(colnames(averages), "\\.?p?\\[\\d+\\]$", "")  # Remove either ".p[XX]" or "[XX]"
)

# Pivot the data into wide format where each metric_name becomes a separate column
averages_wide <- averages %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "full_colname", values_to = "average") %>%
  left_join(column_info, by = "full_colname") %>%
  mutate(participant_id = as.numeric(participant_id)) %>%
  select(participant_id, metric_name, average) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric_name, values_from = average)  # Pivot into wide format
```

```{r}

religiousMatrix <- data.matrix(clean_data_summary[,c("Religiosity", "Spirituality", "AttendChurch", "ReligiousActivity")]) - 1

KMO
KMO$ImCov

evals <- eigen(scree)$values
print(scree, cutoff = "0.3")
scree(scree, factors = F)

#religiousMatrix <- psych::polychoric(religiousMatrix)

#round(EFA$Phi, 3)
(evals/sum(evals)*100)[1:4]
EFA$communalities

religiousMatrix.efa <- fa(religiousMatrix, nfactors = 1, rotate = "oblimin", fm ="ml", cor = "poly", scores = "regression")
print(religiousMatrix.efa)
fa.diagram(religiousMatrix.efa)

print(religiousMatrix.efa$loadings, cutoff = "0.3")
clean_data_summary$ReligiousFactor <- religiousMatrix.efa$scores
# data.religious$ReligiousFactor<- religious.efa$scores
```

```{r}
raw_behavior_path <- "C:/Users/Brian Kim/Documents/OneDrive - Drexel University/Documents/classes/cognew/Neuroethics/IndividualDifferenceRiskBenefit/DATA_ANALYSIS/data/raw_mturk_data/raw.csv"

# Select MFSQ, GRiPS, and Berlin columns
selected_columns <- raw_data %>%
  select(user_id, starts_with("MFSQ"), starts_with("GRiPS"), starts_with("Berlin"))

# Collapse across user_id and take the first value for each column
collapsed_data <- selected_columns %>%
  group_by(user_id) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), first, na.rm = TRUE))

# Perform an inner join to keep only rows with user_id that exist in both datasets
final_table <- final_table %>%
  inner_join(collapsed_data, by = "user_id")
save(final_table, file='final_ddm_ideological_combined.RData')
```


# Ridge Regression

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(glmnet)
library(data.table)

# Define dependent and independent variables
dependent_vars <- c("time", "b_gain", "b_risk", "alpha", "theta", "bias")
independent_formula <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(c("condition", "GRIPS", "consequentalism", "politics", 
                                                    "Harm", "Fairness", "Loyalty", "Authority", "Sanctity", 
                                                    "sex", "poly(age, 2, raw=TRUE)", "BerlinScore", "ReligiousFactor"), 
                                                 collapse = " + ")))

# Ensure final_table is a data.table
setDT(final_table)
# Relevel the 'condition' factor with "Motor Function" as the baseline
final_table[, condition := relevel(factor(condition), ref = "Motor Function")]

# Prepare the design matrix for independent variables using the formula
data_matrix <- model.matrix(independent_formula, data = final_table)[, -1]  # Drop intercept column

# Function to run ridge regression with cross-validation
run_ridge_cv <- function(dep_var) {
  y <- final_table[[dep_var]]
  
  # Perform cross-validated ridge regression
  cv_fit <- cv.glmnet(data_matrix, y, alpha = 0)  # alpha = 0 for ridge
  
  # Best lambda based on cross-validation
  best_lambda <- cv_fit$lambda.min
  
  # Final model using the best lambda
  ridge_model <- glmnet(data_matrix, y, alpha = 0, lambda = best_lambda)
  
  # Return results
  list(dep_var = dep_var, model = ridge_model, best_lambda = best_lambda, cv_fit = cv_fit)
}

# Run ridge regression for each dependent variable and store results
results <- lapply(dependent_vars, run_ridge_cv)

# Access results for each model
for (result in results) {
  cat("Dependent Variable:", result$dep_var, "\n")
  cat("Best Lambda:", result$best_lambda, "\n")
  print(coef(result$model))
  cat("\n")
}
```

# NEW Regression Analysis

This new regression analysis runs many different regressions in a loop so that all coefficients
and p-values can be extracted efficiently.

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)

# Define dependent and independent variables
dependent_vars <- c("time", "b_gain", "b_risk", "alpha", "theta", "bias")
independent_vars <- c("condition", "GRIPS", "consequentalism", "politics", 
                      "Harm", "Fairness", "Loyalty", "Authority", "Sanctity", 
                      "sex", "poly(age, 2, raw=TRUE)", "BerlinScore", "ReligiousFactor")

# Initialize an empty data frame to store the results
results <- data.frame(Independent_Var = character(), 
                      Dependent_Var = character(),
                      Beta = numeric(), 
                      P_Value = numeric(), 
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Loop through each dependent variable
for(dep_var in dependent_vars) {
  # Loop through each independent variable
  for(ind_var in independent_vars) {
    # Create the formula
    formula <- as.formula(paste(dep_var, "~", ind_var))
    
    # Run the linear regression
    model <- lm(formula, data = final_table)
    
    # Extract the beta coefficient and p-value (ignoring intercept)
    summary_model <- summary(model)
    coef_data <- summary_model$coefficients
    
    # Check if independent variable has multiple levels (for factors)
    ind_var_rows <- grep(ind_var, rownames(coef_data))
    
    # Extract beta coefficient(s) and p-value(s) for the independent variable
    for(i in ind_var_rows) {
      beta <- coef_data[i, "Estimate"]
      p_value <- coef_data[i, "Pr(>|t|)"]
      t_value <- coef_data[i, "t value"]
      
      # Store the results in the results data frame
      results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
        Independent_Var = rownames(coef_data)[i],
        Dependent_Var = dep_var,
        Beta = beta,
        P_Value = p_value,
        T_Value = t_value
      ))
    }
  }
}

# Print or inspect the results
print(results)
```

```{r}
save(results, file='final_ddm_regression_results.RData')
```


## Regresson for subscores

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)

# Define dependent and independent variables
dependent_vars <- c("time", "b_gain", "b_risk", "alpha", "theta", "bias")
independent_vars <- c("MFSQ1", "MFSQ2", "MFSQ3", "MFSQ4", "MFSQ5", "MFSQ6", "MFSQ7", "MFSQ8", "MFSQ9", "MFSQ10", "MFSQ11", "MFSQ12", "MFSQ13", "MFSQ14", "MFSQ15", "MFSQ16", "MFSQ17", "MFSQ18", "MFSQ19", "MFSQ20", "MFSQ21", "MFSQ22", "MFSQ23", "MFSQ24", "MFSQ25", "MFSQ26", "MFSQ27", "MFSQ28", "MFSQ29", "MFSQ30", "MFSQ31", "MFSQ32", "GRiPS_1", "GRiPS_2", "GRiPS_3", "GRiPS_4", "GRiPS_5", "GRiPS_6", "GRiPS_7", "GRiPS_8", "Berlin1", "Berlin2", "Berlin3", "Berlin4"  )

# Initialize an empty data frame to store the results
subscore_results <- data.frame(Independent_Var = character(), 
                      Dependent_Var = character(),
                      Beta = numeric(), 
                      P_Value = numeric(), 
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Loop through each dependent variable
for(dep_var in dependent_vars) {
  # Loop through each independent variable
  for(ind_var in independent_vars) {
    # Create the formula
    formula <- as.formula(paste(dep_var, "~", ind_var))
    
    # Run the linear regression
    model <- lm(formula, data = final_table)
    
    # Extract the beta coefficient and p-value (ignoring intercept)
    summary_model <- summary(model)
    coef_data <- summary_model$coefficients
    
    # Check if independent variable has multiple levels (for factors)
    ind_var_rows <- grep(ind_var, rownames(coef_data))
    
    # Extract beta coefficient(s) and p-value(s) for the independent variable
    for(i in ind_var_rows) {
      beta <- coef_data[i, "Estimate"]
      p_value <- coef_data[i, "Pr(>|t|)"]
      t_value <- coef_data[i, "t value"]
      
      # Store the results in the subscore_results data frame
      subscore_results <- rbind(subscore_results, data.frame(
        Independent_Var = rownames(coef_data)[i],
        Dependent_Var = dep_var,
        Beta = beta,
        P_Value = p_value,
        T_Value = t_value
      ))
    }
  }
}

# Print or inspect the results
print(subscore_results)
```

## Correlating Metrics to Each Other

```{r}
library(corrplot)

# Select the relevant columns from final_table
selected_data <- final_table %>%
  select(all_of(independent_vars))

# Compute the correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(selected_data, use = "complete.obs")

# Display the correlation heatmap
corrplot(cor_matrix, method = "color", type = "lower", 
         tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45, 
         col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(200),
         title = "Correlation Heatmap")
```
